title: SvidSigner private key material is never zeroized
description:
persona-core/src/signer.rs:55-61:

    pub struct SvidSigner {
        key_pair: EcdsaKeyPair,
        rng: SystemRandom,
        public_key_der: Vec<u8>,
        /// PKCS#8 DER bytes kept for jsonwebtoken ES256 signing.
        pkcs8_der: Vec<u8>,
    }

`pkcs8_der` is the full PKCS#8 DER of the P-256 private key, held in a plain `Vec<u8>` with no `Drop` impl and no `Zeroizing` wrapper. When `SvidSigner` is dropped the allocation is freed with the private scalar still in it. The doc comment on the struct says "The keypair is never persisted; it is discarded when the process exits" — "discarded" is not what `Vec::drop` does.

Concretely: the key survives in freed heap memory and can reach a core dump, a swap page, or a later heap allocation in the same process. Two copies exist (`pkcs8_der` plus whatever `EcdsaKeyPair` holds internally), and `SvidSigner::new()` at line 67-70 creates a third short-lived one — the `pkcs8` `Document` returned by `generate_pkcs8`, which is `.to_vec()`'d and then dropped un-zeroized at end of scope.

This is a daemon whose entire security argument rests on the ephemeral CA key not escaping the process, so the gap is worth closing even though ring's own `Document` handling is outside our control.

Fix: add `zeroize` and hold the field as `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>`, or store the `EncodingKey` built once at construction and drop the DER immediately. Note `EncodingKey::from_ec_der` is called on every `sign_jwt_svid` (line 110) — building it once in `new()` removes the need to keep the DER around at all, which is the better fix.
close_reason:
Fixed in eb3eddd, and the fix needed no zeroize dependency -- the bead's two suggested fixes were 'add zeroize and hold Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, OR store the EncodingKey built once'. The second is strictly better and the bead already said so; what it did not know is that it makes the first unnecessary.

BEAD IS PARTLY STALE: it describes ring (EcdsaKeyPair, SystemRandom, generate_pkcs8's Document). ring is gone; the signer is p256 now. The 'third short-lived copy' it worried about is the SecretDocument from to_pkcs8_der, which zeroizes on drop, so that one was never a leak.

Measured rather than assumed: every other copy of the private key in the stack already zeroizes -- SigningKey via elliptic-curve, SecretDocument via der/pkcs8, and jsonwebtoken's EncodingKey, which is #[derive(Clone, Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)] (jsonwebtoken-11.0.0/src/encoding.rs:20). persona's own pkcs8_der: Vec<u8> was the single unprotected copy in an otherwise clean stack.

So the field was deleted rather than wrapped. EncodingKey is built once in from_signing_key, straight from the SecretDocument's bytes with no to_vec() in between, so the private key never lands in an unprotected allocation. Building it once is also jsonwebtoken's own documented advice ('This key can be re-used so make sure you only initialize it once if you can for better performance') and removes an EncodingKey::from_ec_der re-parse per token issued.

The known-answer test was NOT weakened: it previously read back the stored pkcs8_der field, and now re-derives the DER from the signing key the signer actually holds, checked against the same TEST_PKCS8_HEX vector. Mutation-verified both ways -- building the EncodingKey from a different key kills jwt_signature_is_sign_raw_of_signing_input, and re-deriving from a fresh key kills known_vector_public_key_and_pkcs8.

Note the struct doc's claim that the keypair 'is discarded when the process exits' is now true of every copy.
